questions.question: How do I build an index without blocking writes on the table?

sentences.text: To build an index without blocking writes, use the CONCURRENTLY option of CREATE INDEX.

citations.quote: specifying the CONCURRENTLY option of CREATE INDEX

sentences.text: PostgreSQL supports building indexes without locking out writes, allowing normal operations to continue while the index is built.

citations.quote: PostgreSQL supports building indexes without locking out writes
allows normal operations to continue while the index is built

sentences.text: The concurrent method performs two scans and waits for existing transactions, so it requires more total work and takes significantly longer to complete.

citations.quote: PostgreSQL must perform two scans of the table
takes significantly longer to complete

sentences.text: Only one concurrent index build can occur on a table at a time, and CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot be performed within a transaction block.

citations.quote: only one concurrent index build can occur on a table at a time
a regular CREATE INDEX command can be performed within a transaction block, but CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot

sentences.text: If a problem arises while scanning the table, CREATE INDEX fails but leaves an invalid index, and the recommended recovery is to drop it and try again to perform CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY.

citations.quote: the CREATE INDEX command will fail but leave behind an “ invalid ” index
drop the index and try again to perform CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY

questions.question: ¿Cómo creo un índice que solo cubra las filas donde una columna no es nula?
Can I index the result of lower(email) to speed up case-insensitive lookups?

sentences.text: Yes: an index column need not be just a column of the underlying table, but can be a function or scalar expression computed from one or more columns of the table.

citations.quote: An index column need not be just a column of the underlying table

sentences.text: For case-insensitive comparisons using lower, the query can use an index if one has been defined on the result of lower(col1).

citations.quote: This query can use an index if one has been defined on the result of the lower(col1) function

sentences.text: Such an expression index is relatively expensive to maintain, but the index expressions are not recomputed during an indexed search.

citations.quote: Index expressions are relatively expensive to maintain
the index expressions are not recomputed during an indexed search

questions.question: ¿Qué tipo de índice conviene para columnas de fecha en tablas muy grandes insertadas en orden?
Which index types support containment queries on jsonb columns?

sentences.text: GIN indexes can be used to efficiently search for keys or key/value pairs occurring within a large number of jsonb documents.

citations.quote: GIN indexes can be used to efficiently search for keys or key/value pairs occurring within a large number of jsonb documents

sentences.text: For jsonb containment queries, the default GIN operator class supports the containment operator @>.

citations.quote: The default GIN operator class for jsonb supports queries with the key-exists operators ? , ?| and ?& , the containment operator @>

sentences.text: The non-default GIN operator class jsonb_path_ops does not support the key-exists operators, but it does support @>, @? and @@.

citations.quote: The non-default GIN operator class jsonb_path_ops does not support the key-exists operators, but it does support @> , @? and @@

questions.question: ¿Qué diferencia hay entre VACUUM y VACUUM FULL?

sentences.text: El VACUUM normal, sin FULL, simplemente recupera espacio y lo deja disponible para reutilizarse.

citations.quote: simply reclaims space and makes it available for re-use

sentences.text: Ese VACUUM normal puede operar en paralelo con la lectura y escritura normal de la tabla, ya que no se obtiene un bloqueo exclusivo.

citations.quote: can operate in parallel with normal reading and writing of the table

sentences.text: En cambio, VACUUM FULL reescribe todo el contenido de la tabla en un nuevo archivo de disco sin espacio extra, lo que permite devolver al sistema operativo el espacio no usado.

citations.quote: rewrites the entire contents of the table into a new disk file with no extra space

sentences.text: VACUUM FULL es mucho más lento y requiere un bloqueo ACCESS EXCLUSIVE en cada tabla mientras se está procesando.

citations.quote: requires an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on each table while it is being processed

questions.question: Why does PostgreSQL need to vacuum to prevent transaction ID wraparound?

sentences.text: PostgreSQL's MVCC semantics depend on comparing transaction IDs, and a long-running cluster can suffer transaction ID wraparound when the XID counter wraps to zero, making past transactions appear to be in the future and causing catastrophic data loss.

citations.quote: MVCC transaction semantics depend on being able to compare transaction ID
a cluster that runs for a long time (more than 4 billion transactions) would suffer transaction ID wraparound
the XID counter wraps around to zero
transactions that were in the past appear to be in the future
In short, catastrophic data loss.

sentences.text: To avoid this, every table in every database must be vacuumed at least once every two billion transactions.

citations.quote: it is necessary to vacuum every table in every database at least once every two billion transactions

sentences.text: VACUUM prevents the problem by marking rows as frozen, meaning they were inserted by a transaction committed sufficiently far in the past that their effects are certain to be visible to all current and future transactions.

citations.quote: VACUUM will mark rows as frozen
indicating that they were inserted by a transaction that committed sufficiently far in the past
the effects of the inserting transaction are certain to be visible to all current and future transactions

sentences.text: Frozen row versions are treated as if the inserting XID were FrozenTransactionId, which is always considered older than every normal XID, so they appear to be in the past to all normal transactions regardless of wraparound issues.

citations.quote: Frozen row versions are treated as if the inserting XID were FrozenTransactionId
which does not follow the normal XID comparison rules
always considered older than every normal XID
to all normal transactions regardless of wraparound issues

questions.question: ¿Cómo veo el plan de ejecución real de una consulta con tiempos y filas?

sentences.text: Para ver el plan de ejecución real se usa la opción ANALYZE de EXPLAIN, que ejecuta realmente la consulta.

citations.quote: EXPLAIN actually executes the query

sentences.text: Con esa opción se muestran los recuentos reales de filas y el tiempo real acumulado en cada nodo del plan, junto con las mismas estimaciones que muestra un EXPLAIN normal.

citations.quote: displays the true row counts and true run time accumulated within each plan node
along with the same estimates that a plain EXPLAIN shows

sentences.text: La documentación advierte que la sentencia se ejecuta realmente cuando se usa la opción ANALYZE y que otros efectos secundarios de la sentencia ocurrirán como de costumbre.

citations.quote: the statement is actually executed when the ANALYZE option is used
other side effects of the statement will happen as usual

questions.question: What anomalies are prevented at the Repeatable Read isolation level?

sentences.text: Repeatable Read prevents all of the phenomena described in Table 13.1 except for serialization anomalies.

citations.quote: prevents all of the phenomena described in Table 13.1 except for serialization anomalies

questions.question: ¿Qué nivel de aislamiento usa PostgreSQL por defecto?
How do I lock a row so other transactions cannot update it until I commit?

sentences.text: Use SELECT FOR UPDATE to lock the rows retrieved by a SELECT statement as though for update.

citations.quote: FOR UPDATE causes the rows retrieved by the SELECT statement to be locked as though for update.

sentences.text: This prevents those rows from being locked, modified or deleted by other transactions until the current transaction ends.

citations.quote: This prevents them from being locked, modified or deleted by other transactions until the current transaction ends.

sentences.text: SELECT FOR UPDATE temporarily blocks other transactions from executing an UPDATE or DELETE that would affect the locked row.

citations.quote: SELECT FOR UPDATE temporarily blocks other transactions from acquiring the same lock or executing an UPDATE or DELETE which would affect the locked row

sentences.text: After the transaction holding the lock commits or rolls back, a blocked transaction will proceed with the conflicting operation unless an actual UPDATE of the row was performed while the lock was held.

citations.quote: but once the transaction holding this lock commits or rolls back, a blocked transaction will proceed with the conflicting operation unless an actual UPDATE of the row was performed while the lock was held.

questions.question: ¿Cómo particiono una tabla por rango de fechas?

sentences.text: Para particionar una tabla por rango de fechas, se declara como tabla particionada usando una cláusula como PARTITION BY RANGE (logdate).

citations.quote: PARTITION BY RANGE (logdate)

sentences.text: La declaración incluye el método de particionamiento y la lista de columnas o expresiones que se usarán como clave de partición.

citations.quote: The declaration includes the partitioning method as described above, plus a list of columns or expressions to be used as the partition key

sentences.text: Cada partición debe especificar límites que correspondan al método de particionamiento y a la clave de partición del padre.

citations.quote: Each partition's definition must specify bounds that correspond to the partitioning method and partition key of the parent.

sentences.text: En el particionamiento por rango no debe haber solapamiento entre los rangos de valores asignados a particiones diferentes.

citations.quote: with no overlap between the ranges of values assigned to different partitions

sentences.text: Los límites de cada rango son inclusivos en el extremo inferior y exclusivos en el extremo superior.

citations.quote: Each range's bounds are understood as being inclusive at the lower end and exclusive at the upper end.

sentences.text: Para definir los límites de una partición de rango se usa FOR VALUES FROM ('2016-07-01') TO ('2016-08-01');

questions.question: How do I write a recursive query to walk a parent-child hierarchy?

sentences.text: Use WITH RECURSIVE to write a query that walks hierarchical or tree-structured data.

citations.quote: Recursive queries are typically used to deal with hierarchical or tree-structured data.

sentences.text: A recursive WITH query has a non-recursive term, then UNION or UNION ALL, then a recursive term that can reference the query's own output.

citations.quote: The general form of a recursive WITH query is always a non-recursive term
where only the recursive term can contain a reference to the query's own output

sentences.text: The recursive self-reference must appear on the right-hand side of the UNION, and only one recursive self-reference is permitted per query.

citations.quote: where the recursive self-reference must appear on the right-hand side of the UNION
Only one recursive self-reference is permitted per query.

sentences.text: The documentation's hierarchy example uses WITH RECURSIVE included_parts(sub_part, part, quantity) AS and recursively joins included_parts to parts with the condition p.part = pr.sub_part.

citations.quote: WITH RECURSIVE included_parts(sub_part, part, quantity) AS
WHERE p.part = pr.sub_part

sentences.text: Ensure that the recursive part eventually returns no tuples, or the query will loop indefinitely.

citations.quote: Be sure that the recursive part of the query will eventually return no tuples, or else the query will loop indefinitely.

questions.question: ¿Cómo calculo un total acumulado por cliente con funciones de ventana?

sentences.text: Para calcular un total acumulado, puedes usar una función de agregado como función de ventana con ORDER BY; la documentación señala que un agregado usado con ORDER BY y la definición de marco de ventana predeterminada produce un comportamiento de “running sum”.

citations.quote: An aggregate used with ORDER BY and the default window frame definition produces a “ running sum ” type of behavior

sentences.text: Para hacerlo por cliente, usa PARTITION BY con la expresión que identifica al cliente, ya que PARTITION BY divide las filas en grupos o particiones que comparten los mismos valores.

citations.quote: The PARTITION BY clause within OVER divides the rows into groups, or partitions, that share the same values of the PARTITION BY expression(s).

sentences.text: Con ORDER BY, el marco predeterminado abarca desde el inicio de la partición hasta la fila actual, más las filas siguientes que sean iguales a la fila actual según ORDER BY.

citations.quote: By default, if ORDER BY is supplied then the frame consists of all rows from the start of the partition up through the current row, plus any following rows that are equal to the current row according to the ORDER BY clause.

sentences.text: Si quieres la agregación sobre toda la partición, omite ORDER BY o usa ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING.

citations.quote: To obtain aggregation over the whole partition, omit ORDER BY or use ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING

sentences.text: La función debe invocarse con sintaxis de función de ventana, es decir, se requiere una cláusula OVER.

citations.quote: an OVER clause is required

questions.question: What is the difference between json and jsonb?

sentences.text: The json type stores an exact copy of the input text, which processing functions must reparse on each execution.

citations.quote: stores an exact copy of the input text

sentences.text: The jsonb type is stored in a decomposed binary format that is slightly slower to input but significantly faster to process because no reparsing is needed.

citations.quote: decomposed binary format that makes it slightly slower to input
significantly faster to process, since no reparsing is needed

sentences.text: jsonb also supports indexing, which can be a significant advantage.

citations.quote: jsonb also supports indexing, which can be a significant advantage

sentences.text: The json type preserves semantically-insignificant white space between tokens and the order of keys within JSON objects, and it keeps all duplicate key/value pairs.

citations.quote: it will preserve semantically-insignificant white space between tokens, as well as the order of keys within JSON objects
all the key/value pairs are kept

sentences.text: By contrast, jsonb does not preserve white space, does not preserve the order of object keys, and does not keep duplicate object keys.

citations.quote: jsonb does not preserve white space, does not preserve the order of object keys, and does not keep duplicate object keys

sentences.text: Most applications should prefer to store JSON data as jsonb unless there are quite specialized needs, such as legacy assumptions about ordering of object keys.

citations.quote: most applications should prefer to store JSON data as jsonb
unless there are quite specialized needs, such as legacy assumptions about ordering of object keys

sentences.text: jsonb will reject numbers outside the range of the PostgreSQL numeric data type, while json will not.

citations.quote: jsonb will reject numbers that are outside the range of the PostgreSQL numeric data type, while json will not

sentences.text: The jsonb input function rejects \u0000 and disallows Unicode escapes for characters that cannot be represented in the database encoding.

citations.quote: The jsonb type also rejects \u0000 (because that cannot be represented in PostgreSQL 's text type)
it disallows Unicode escapes for characters that cannot be represented in the database encoding

questions.question: ¿Cómo convierto un documento JSON en filas y columnas con JSON_TABLE?

sentences.text: JSON_TABLE es una función SQL/JSON que consulta datos JSON y presenta los resultados como una vista relacional que puede usarse como una tabla SQL normal.

citations.quote: JSON_TABLE is an SQL/JSON function which queries JSON data and presents the results as a relational view

sentences.text: Puede usarse dentro de la cláusula FROM de un SELECT, UPDATE o DELETE y como fuente de datos en una sentencia MERGE.

citations.quote: You can use JSON_TABLE inside the FROM clause of a SELECT , UPDATE , or DELETE and as data source in a MERGE statement.

sentences.text: Tomando datos JSON como entrada, JSON_TABLE usa una expresión de ruta JSON para extraer una parte de los datos proporcionados y usarla como patrón de fila para la vista construida.

citations.quote: Taking JSON data as input, JSON_TABLE uses a JSON path expression to extract a part of the provided data to use as a row pattern for the constructed view.

sentences.text: Cada valor SQL/JSON dado por el patrón de fila sirve como fuente para una fila separada en la vista construida.

citations.quote: Each SQL/JSON value given by the row pattern serves as source for a separate row in the constructed view.

sentences.text: Para dividir el patrón de fila en columnas, JSON_TABLE proporciona la cláusula COLUMNS que define el esquema de la vista creada.

citations.quote: To split the row pattern into columns, JSON_TABLE provides the COLUMNS clause that defines the schema of the created view.

sentences.text: Para cada columna, se puede especificar una expresión de ruta JSON separada que se evalúa contra el patrón de fila para obtener el valor SQL/JSON que será el valor de esa columna en una fila de salida.

citations.quote: For each column, a separate JSON path expression can be specified to be evaluated against the row pattern to get an SQL/JSON value that will become the value for the specified column in a given output row.

sentences.text: Los datos JSON anidados pueden extraerse con la cláusula NESTED PATH, y cada cláusula NESTED PATH puede generar una o más columnas usando los datos de un nivel anidado del patrón de fila.

citations.quote: JSON data stored at a nested level of the row pattern can be extracted using the NESTED PATH clause.
Each NESTED PATH clause can be used to generate one or more columns using the data from a nested level of the row pattern.

sentences.text: Las filas producidas por JSON_TABLE se unen lateralmente a la fila que las generó, por lo que no hay que unir explícitamente la vista construida con la tabla original que contiene los datos JSON.

citations.quote: The rows produced by JSON_TABLE are laterally joined to the row that generated them, so you do not have to explicitly join the constructed view with the original table holding JSON data.

questions.question: Can MERGE return the rows it inserted or updated?

sentences.text: Yes. MERGE can return data from the rows it inserts, updates, or deletes through its optional RETURNING clause.

citations.quote: The optional RETURNING clause causes MERGE to compute and return value(s) based on each row inserted, updated, or deleted.

sentences.text: For MERGE, the data available to RETURNING is the content of the source row plus the content of the inserted, updated, or deleted target row.

citations.quote: the content of the source row plus the content of the inserted, updated, or deleted target row

sentences.text: The merge_action() function may be used in the RETURNING list of a MERGE command to identify the action taken for each row, which will be INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE.

citations.quote: may be used in the RETURNING list of a MERGE command to identify the action taken for each row
This will be 'INSERT' , 'UPDATE' , or 'DELETE' .

questions.question: ¿Cómo hago un upsert con INSERT ... ON CONFLICT?

sentences.text: La cláusula opcional ON CONFLICT especifica una acción alternativa a generar un error por violación de unicidad o de restricción de exclusión.

citations.quote: The optional ON CONFLICT clause specifies an alternative action to raising a unique violation or exclusion constraint violation error

sentences.text: La acción puede ser DO NOTHING, que simplemente evita insertar la fila, o DO UPDATE, que actualiza la fila existente que entra en conflicto con la fila propuesta para inserción.

citations.quote: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING simply avoids inserting a row as its alternative action
ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE updates the existing row that conflicts with the row proposed for insertion

sentences.text: Para ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE se debe proporcionar un conflict_target.

citations.quote: For ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE , a conflict_target must be provided

sentences.text: El conflict_target puede realizar inferencia de índice único o nombrar una restricción explícitamente.

citations.quote: conflict_target can perform unique index inference
Either performs unique index inference , or names a constraint explicitly

sentences.text: ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE garantiza un resultado atómico de INSERT o UPDATE, y esto también se conoce como UPSERT.

citations.quote: ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE guarantees an atomic INSERT or UPDATE outcome
This is also known as UPSERT

sentences.text: En modo Read Committed, cada fila propuesta para inserción se insertará o actualizará, y salvo errores no relacionados se garantiza uno de esos dos resultados.

citations.quote: In Read Committed mode, each row proposed for insertion will either insert or update
Unless there are unrelated errors, one of those two outcomes is guaranteed

sentences.text: Las cláusulas SET y WHERE de ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE pueden acceder a la fila existente mediante el nombre de la tabla (o un alias) y a la fila propuesta mediante la tabla especial excluded.

citations.quote: The SET and WHERE clauses in ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE have access to the existing row using the table's name (or an alias), and to the row proposed for insertion using the special excluded table

sentences.text: Como limitación, en tablas remotas INSERT con ON CONFLICT no admite especificar el objetivo del conflicto y, por ello, ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE no está soportado allí porque la especificación es obligatoria.

citations.quote: INSERT with an ON CONFLICT clause does not support specifying the conflict target
ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE is not supported, since the specification is mandatory there

questions.question: How can COPY skip rows with malformed values instead of failing?

sentences.text: Use the ON_ERROR option with an error_action value of ignore to discard the input row and continue with the next one instead of failing the command.

citations.quote: ignore means discard the input row and continue with the next one

sentences.text: A NOTICE message containing the ignored row count is emitted at the end of COPY FROM if at least one row was discarded.

citations.quote: A NOTICE message containing the ignored row count is emitted at the end of the COPY FROM if at least one row was discarded.

questions.question: ¿Cómo cargo un archivo CSV en una tabla con COPY?

sentences.text: La opción FORMAT selecciona el formato de datos que se va a leer o escribir, incluido csv.

citations.quote: Selects the data format to be read or written: text , csv (Comma Separated Values), or binary .

sentences.text: Un ejemplo de carga de un archivo CSV es COPY postgres_log FROM '/full/path/to/logfile.csv' WITH csv;.

citations.quote: COPY postgres_log FROM '/full/path/to/logfile.csv' WITH csv;

sentences.text: El archivo de origen debe estar disponible en la máquina que ejecuta el proceso backend, no en el cliente, porque el backend lee el archivo directamente.

citations.quote: where the file name for the source file must be available on the machine running the backend process, not the client, since the backend process reads the file directly.

sentences.text: En formato CSV, el delimitador predeterminado es una coma.

citations.quote: The default is a tab character in text format, a comma in CSV format.

questions.question: What is the write-ahead log used for?

sentences.text: Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) is a standard method for ensuring data integrity.

citations.quote: a standard method for ensuring data integrity

sentences.text: WAL's central concept is that changes to data files must be written only after WAL records describing the changes have been flushed to permanent storage.

citations.quote: changes to data files (where tables and indexes reside) must be written only after those changes have been logged

sentences.text: After a crash, the database can be recovered using the log by redoing changes that have not been applied to the data pages.

citations.quote: we will be able to recover the database using the log

sentences.text: Only the WAL file needs to be flushed to disk to guarantee that a transaction is committed.

citations.quote: only the WAL file needs to be flushed to disk to guarantee that a transaction is committed

sentences.text: WAL also makes it possible to support on-line backup and point-in-time recovery.

citations.quote: WAL also makes it possible to support on-line backup and point-in-time recovery

questions.question: ¿Cómo configuro la recuperación a un punto en el tiempo (PITR)?

sentences.text: En PostgreSQL 12 y posteriores, PITR se configura usando parámetros normales de configuración del servidor, establecidos en postgresql.conf o mediante ALTER SYSTEM.

citations.quote: On PostgreSQL 12 and above, archive recovery, streaming replication, and PITR are configured using normal server configuration parameters
These are set in postgresql.conf or via ALTER SYSTEM like any other parameter.

sentences.text: Debes especificar restore_command, que indica a PostgreSQL cómo recuperar los segmentos de WAL archivados.

citations.quote: The one thing that you absolutely must specify is the restore_command
which tells PostgreSQL how to retrieve archived WAL file segments

sentences.text: restore_command puede contener %f, sustituido por el nombre del archivo WAL, y %p, sustituido por la ruta de copia del archivo WAL.

citations.quote: It can contain %f , which is replaced by the name of the desired WAL file, and %p , which is replaced by the path name to copy the WAL file to.

sentences.text: El punto de parada, llamado recovery target, se puede especificar por fecha/hora, por punto de restauración con nombre o por finalización de un ID de transacción específico.

citations.quote: either by date/time, named restore point or by completion of a specific transaction ID

sentences.text: Como máximo se puede usar uno de recovery_target, recovery_target_lsn, recovery_target_name, recovery_target_time o recovery_target_xid, y estos parámetros solo se pueden establecer al iniciar el servidor.

citations.quote: At most one of recovery_target , recovery_target_lsn , recovery_target_name , recovery_target_time , or recovery_target_xid can be used
These parameters can only be set at server start.

sentences.text: Para usar un punto de restauración con nombre, recovery_target_name especifica el punto creado con pg_create_restore_point().

citations.quote: the named restore point (created with pg_create_restore_point() )
Creates a named marker record in the write-ahead log that can later be used as a recovery target

sentences.text: El punto de parada debe ser posterior a la hora de finalización de la copia base, es decir, al final de pg_backup_stop.

citations.quote: The stop point must be after the ending time of the base backup
the end time of pg_backup_stop

sentences.text: El parámetro recovery_target_action controla qué hace el servidor al alcanzar el objetivo: por defecto pause pausa la recuperación, promote la finaliza y acepta conexiones, y shutdown detiene el servidor.

citations.quote: The default is pause , which means recovery will be paused.
promote means the recovery process will finish and the server will start to accept connections.
shutdown will stop the server after reaching the recovery target.

sentences.text: El archivo recovery.conf ya no se usa: su soporte se eliminó en PostgreSQL 12 y el servidor no arrancará si existe.

citations.quote: Support for this file was removed in PostgreSQL 12.
The server will not start if a recovery.conf exists.

sources.title: O.1. recovery.conf file merged into postgresql.conf

questions.question: How do I take an incremental backup with pg_basebackup?

sentences.text: You can use pg_basebackup to take an incremental backup by specifying the --incremental option.

citations.quote: You can use pg_basebackup to take an incremental backup by specifying the --incremental option.

sentences.text: You must supply the backup manifest of an earlier backup from the same server as the argument to --incremental.

citations.quote: You must supply, as an argument to --incremental , the backup manifest to an earlier backup from the same server.

sentences.text: WAL summarization must be enabled in order to perform an incremental backup.

citations.quote: a feature which must be enabled in order to perform an incremental backup

sentences.text: An incremental backup cannot be used directly; pg_combinebackup must first be used to combine it with the previous backups upon which it depends.

citations.quote: An incremental backup cannot be used directly; instead, pg_combinebackup must first be used to combine it with the previous backups upon which it depends.

sentences.text: The --incremental option only works with server version 17 and later.

citations.quote: incremental backup ( --incremental ) only works with server version 17 and later

questions.question: ¿Qué hace pg_combinebackup?

sentences.text: pg_combinebackup se utiliza para reconstruir una copia de seguridad completa sintética a partir de una copia de seguridad incremental y las copias anteriores de las que depende.

citations.quote: pg_combinebackup is used to reconstruct a synthetic full backup from an incremental backup and the earlier backups upon which it depends.

sentences.text: Todas las copias de seguridad requeridas deben especificarse en la línea de comandos de la más antigua a la más reciente; la primera debe ser la ruta a la copia completa y la última la ruta a la copia incremental final que se desea restaurar.

citations.quote: Specify all of the required backups on the command line from oldest to newest.
the first backup directory should be the path to the full backup
the last should be the path to the final incremental backup that you wish to restore

sentences.text: La copia reconstruida se escribe en el directorio de salida especificado con la opción -o.

citations.quote: The reconstructed backup will be written to the output directory specified by the -o option.

sentences.text: pg_combinebackup intenta verificar que las copias especificadas formen una cadena de copias de seguridad legal de la que se pueda reconstruir una copia completa correcta.

citations.quote: will attempt to verify that the backups you specify form a legal backup chain from which a correct full backup can be reconstructed

questions.question: How do I set up logical replication of a single table to another server?

sentences.text: Logical replication uses a publish and subscribe model with one or more subscribers subscribing to one or more publications on a publisher node.

citations.quote: Logical replication uses a publish and subscribe model with one or more subscribers subscribing to one or more publications on a publisher node.

sentences.text: It allows replication of data changes on a per-table basis.

citations.quote: Logical replication allows replication of data changes on a per-table basis.

sentences.text: Publishers are servers that do CREATE PUBLICATION, and subscribers are servers that do CREATE SUBSCRIPTION.

citations.quote: publishers (servers that do CREATE PUBLICATION ) replicate data to subscribers (servers that do CREATE SUBSCRIPTION )

sentences.text: Logical replication of a table typically starts with taking a snapshot of the data on the publisher database and copying that to the subscriber.

citations.quote: Logical replication of a table typically starts with taking a snapshot of the data on the publisher database and copying that to the subscriber.

sentences.text: Once that is done, changes on the publisher are sent to the subscriber as they occur in real time.

citations.quote: Once that is done, changes on the publisher are sent to the subscriber as they occur in real time.

sentences.text: The subscriber applies data in the order in which commits were made on the publisher so that transactional consistency is guaranteed for the publications within any single subscription.

questions.question: ¿Cómo convierto una réplica física en suscriptora lógica con pg_createsubscriber?

sentences.text: Para convertir una réplica física en una réplica lógica, ejecuta pg_createsubscriber en el servidor destino; por ejemplo, para las bases hr y finance desde la réplica física en foo:

citations.quote: pg_createsubscriber creates a new logical replica from a physical standby server.
It must be run at the target server.

sentences.text: El comando de ejemplo es: pg_createsubscriber -D /usr/local/pgsql/data -P "host=foo" -d hr -d finance.

citations.quote: pg_createsubscriber -D /usr/local/pgsql/data -P "host=foo" -d hr -d finance

sentences.text: Se incluyen todas las tablas de las bases especificadas y se crea un par de publicación y suscripción para cada base.

citations.quote: All tables in the specified database are included in the logical replication setup.
A pair of publication and subscription objects are created for each database.

sentences.text: pg_createsubscriber no copia los datos iniciales de las tablas; solo hace la fase de sincronización.

citations.quote: pg_createsubscriber does not copy the initial table data.
It does only the synchronization phase

sentences.text: Como prerrequisitos, el servidor origen y el destino deben tener la misma versión mayor que pg_createsubscriber, y el directorio de datos destino debe tener el mismo identificador de sistema que el directorio de datos origen.

citations.quote: The source and target servers must have the same major version as the pg_createsubscriber .
The given target data directory must have the same system identifier as the source data directory.

sentences.text: El servidor destino debe usarse como standby físico y el servidor origen no debe estar en recuperación; además, el origen debe tener wal_level en logical.

citations.quote: The target server must be used as a physical standby.
The source server must not be in recovery.
The source server must have wal_level as logical .

sentences.text: También se exige que el destino acepte conexiones locales y que el origen acepte conexiones desde el destino.

citations.quote: The target server must accept local connections.
The source server must accept connections from the target server.

questions.question: How does streaming replication to a standby server work?

sentences.text: Streaming replication allows a standby server to stay more up-to-date than is possible with file-based log shipping.

citations.quote: Streaming replication allows a standby server to stay more up-to-date than is possible with file-based log shipping.

sentences.text: The standby connects to the primary, which streams WAL records to the standby as they're generated, without waiting for the WAL file to be filled.

citations.quote: The standby connects to the primary, which streams WAL records to the standby as they're generated, without waiting for the WAL file to be filled.

sentences.text: Streaming replication is asynchronous by default, so there is a small delay between committing a transaction in the primary and the changes becoming visible in the standby.

citations.quote: Streaming replication is asynchronous by default
there is a small delay between committing a transaction in the primary and the changes becoming visible in the standby

sentences.text: To configure it, a file-based log-shipping standby server is set up, and then primary_conninfo is set to point to the primary server.

citations.quote: To use streaming replication, set up a file-based log-shipping standby server
setting the primary_conninfo setting to point to the primary server

sentences.text: When the standby is started and primary_conninfo is set correctly, the standby will connect to the primary after replaying all WAL files available in the archive.

citations.quote: When the standby is started and primary_conninfo is set correctly, the standby will connect to the primary after replaying all WAL files available in the archive.

questions.question: ¿Cómo permito conexiones con contraseña desde una red específica en pg_hba.conf?

TYPE  DATABASE        USER            ADDRESS                 METHOD

citations.quote: The method password sends the password in clear-text

citations.quote: Since the pg_hba.conf records are examined sequentially for each connection attempt, the order of the records is significant.

questions.question: How do I restrict which rows each user can see with row-level security?

sentences.text: Row security policies restrict, on a per-user basis, which rows can be returned by normal queries or modified by data modification commands.

citations.quote: tables can have row security policies that restrict, on a per-user basis, which rows can be returned

sentences.text: To apply created policies, row-level security must be enabled on the table using ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY.

citations.quote: row-level security must be enabled on the table (using ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY )

sentences.text: Policies are created using the CREATE POLICY command.

citations.quote: Policies are created using the CREATE POLICY command

sentences.text: A policy grants the permission to select, insert, update, or delete rows that match the relevant policy expression.

citations.quote: A policy grants the permission to select, insert, update, or delete rows that match the relevant policy expression

sentences.text: Existing table rows are checked against the expression specified in USING.

citations.quote: Existing table rows are checked against the expression specified in USING

sentences.text: When a USING expression returns true for a given row then that row is visible to the user, while if false or null is returned then the row is not visible.

citations.quote: When a USING expression returns true for a given row then that row is visible to the user, while if false or null is returned then the row is not visible

sentences.text: Row security policies can be specific to commands, or to roles, or to both.

citations.quote: Row security policies can be specific to commands, or to roles, or to both

sentences.text: If no role is specified, or the special user name PUBLIC is used, then the policy applies to all users on the system.

citations.quote: If no role is specified, or the special user name PUBLIC is used, then the policy applies to all users on the system

sentences.text: If no policy exists for the table, a default-deny policy is used, meaning that no rows are visible or can be modified.

citations.quote: If no policy exists for the table, a default-deny policy is used, meaning that no rows are visible or can be modified

sentences.text: Superusers and roles with the BYPASSRLS attribute always bypass the row security system when accessing a table, and table owners normally bypass row security as well.

citations.quote: Superusers and roles with the BYPASSRLS attribute always bypass the row security system when accessing a table
Table owners normally bypass row security as well

sentences.text: Enabling and disabling row security, as well as adding policies to a table, is always the privilege of the table owner only.

citations.quote: Enabling and disabling row security, as well as adding policies to a table, is always the privilege of the table owner only

questions.question: ¿Cómo escribo un trigger en PL/pgSQL que registre cambios en una tabla de auditoría?

sentences.text: La documentación presenta el Ejemplo 41.4 como un ejemplo de función de trigger de auditoría en PL/pgSQL.

citations.quote: Example 41.4 shows an example of an audit trigger function in PL/pgSQL

sentences.text: Ese ejemplo asegura que cualquier insert, update o delete de una fila de la tabla emp se registre (es decir, se audite) en la tabla emp_audit.

citations.quote: any insert, update or delete of a row in the emp table is recorded (i.e., audited) in the emp_audit table

sentences.text: Se define una función process_emp_audit() que RETURNS TRIGGER.

citations.quote: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION process_emp_audit() RETURNS TRIGGER AS $emp_audit$

sentences.text: La función usa la variable especial TG_OP para determinar la operación.

citations.quote: making use of the special variable TG_OP to work out the operation

sentences.text: Para DELETE, UPDATE e INSERT, la función inserta en emp_audit usando now(), current_user y OLD.* o NEW.* según corresponda.

citations.quote: INSERT INTO emp_audit SELECT 'D', now(), current_user, OLD.*;
INSERT INTO emp_audit SELECT 'U', now(), current_user, NEW.*;
INSERT INTO emp_audit SELECT 'I', now(), current_user, NEW.*;

sentences.text: La función termina con RETURN NULL, porque el resultado se ignora al ser un trigger AFTER.

citations.quote: RETURN NULL; -- result is ignored since this is an AFTER trigger

sentences.text: El trigger se crea como AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON emp, FOR EACH ROW, ejecutando process_emp_audit().

citations.quote: AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON emp
FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION process_emp_audit();

questions.question: How do I rank full-text search results by relevance?

sentences.text: Ranking attempts to measure how relevant documents are to a particular query, so that when there are many matches the most relevant ones can be shown first.

citations.quote: Ranking attempts to measure how relevant documents are to a particular query

sentences.text: PostgreSQL provides two predefined ranking functions, which take into account lexical, proximity, and structural information.

citations.quote: PostgreSQL provides two predefined ranking functions, which take into account lexical, proximity, and structural information

sentences.text: The two ranking functions currently available are ts_rank and ts_rank_cd.

citations.quote: The two ranking functions currently available are
ts_rank([ weights float4[] , ] vector tsvector , query tsquery [ , normalization integer ]) returns float4
ts_rank_cd([ weights float4[] , ] vector tsvector , query tsquery [ , normalization integer ]) returns float4

sentences.text: ts_rank ranks vectors based on the frequency of their matching lexemes.

citations.quote: Ranks vectors based on the frequency of their matching lexemes

sentences.text: ts_rank_cd computes the cover density ranking for the given document vector and query.

citations.quote: This function computes the cover density ranking for the given document vector and query

sentences.text: Cover density is similar to ts_rank ranking except that the proximity of matching lexemes to each other is taken into consideration.

citations.quote: Cover density is similar to ts_rank ranking except that the proximity of matching lexemes to each other is taken into consideration

sentences.text: For both these functions, the optional weights argument offers the ability to weigh word instances more or less heavily depending on how they are labeled.

citations.quote: For both these functions, the optional weights argument offers the ability to weigh word instances more or less heavily depending on how they are labeled

sentences.text: Both ranking functions take an integer normalization option that specifies whether and how a document's length should impact its rank.

citations.quote: Both ranking functions take an integer normalization option that specifies whether and how a document's length should impact its rank

sentences.text: An example selects only the ten highest-ranked matches and uses ORDER BY rank DESC LIMIT 10.

citations.quote: Here is an example that selects only the ten highest-ranked matches
ORDER BY rank DESC LIMIT 10

sentences.text: Ranking can be expensive since it requires consulting the tsvector of each matching document, which can be I/O bound and therefore slow.

citations.quote: Ranking can be expensive since it requires consulting the tsvector of each matching document, which can be I/O bound and therefore slow

questions.question: ¿Qué es un tsvector y para qué sirve?

sentences.text: PostgreSQL ofrece dos tipos de datos diseñados para soportar búsqueda de texto completo, y el tipo tsvector representa un documento en una forma optimizada para la búsqueda de texto.

citations.quote: PostgreSQL provides two data types that are designed to support full text search
The tsvector type represents a document in a form optimized for text search

sentences.text: Se proporciona un tipo de datos tsvector para almacenar documentos preprocesados.

citations.quote: A data type tsvector is provided for storing preprocessed documents

sentences.text: Un valor tsvector es una lista ordenada de lexemas distintos, que son palabras que han sido normalizadas para fusionar diferentes variantes de la misma palabra.

citations.quote: A tsvector value is a sorted list of distinct lexemes
which are words that have been normalized to merge different variants of the same word

sentences.text: La ordenación y la eliminación de duplicados se realizan automáticamente durante la entrada.

citations.quote: Sorting and duplicate-elimination are done automatically during input

sentences.text: El tipo tsvector en sí no realiza ninguna normalización de palabras; normalmente el texto sin procesar de un documento debe pasarse por to_tsvector para normalizar las palabras adecuadamente para la búsqueda.

citations.quote: the tsvector type itself does not perform any word normalization
Raw document text should usually be passed through to_tsvector to normalize the words appropriately for searching

sentences.text: La búsqueda y la clasificación se realizan enteramente sobre la representación tsvector de un documento.

citations.quote: Searching and ranking are performed entirely on the tsvector representation of a document

questions.question: How do I refresh a materialized view without blocking reads?

sentences.text: To refresh without blocking concurrent reads, use REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY, which will "Refresh the materialized view without locking out concurrent selects on the materialized view."

citations.quote: Even with this option only one REFRESH at a time may run against any one materialized view.

questions.question: ¿Cómo defino una columna identidad en lugar de serial?

sentences.text: Para crear una columna identidad, se usa la cláusula GENERATED ... AS IDENTITY en CREATE TABLE.

GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY

citations.quote: The data types smallserial , serial and bigserial are not true types, but merely a notational convenience for creating unique identifier columns

citations.quote: Another way is to use the SQL-standard identity column feature

questions.question: Can a generated column be virtual instead of stored in PostgreSQL 17?

sentences.text: There are two kinds of generated columns: stored and virtual.

citations.quote: PostgreSQL currently implements only stored generated columns.

questions.question: ¿Cómo envío notificaciones entre sesiones con LISTEN y NOTIFY?

sentences.text: Para enviar notificaciones entre sesiones, una sesión se registra como oyente en un canal de notificación con LISTEN.

citations.quote: LISTEN registers the current session as a listener on the notification channel named channel

sentences.text: Cuando se ejecuta NOTIFY channel, se notifica a todas las sesiones que están escuchando ese canal.

citations.quote: all the sessions currently listening on that notification channel are notified

sentences.text: NOTIFY envía un evento de notificación, junto con una cadena payload opcional, a cada aplicación cliente que previamente ejecutó LISTEN channel para el nombre de canal especificado.

citations.quote: The NOTIFY command sends a notification event together with an optional “ payload ” string
has previously executed LISTEN channel for the specified channel name

sentences.text: La información que recibe el cliente incluye el nombre del canal, el PID del proceso servidor de la sesión notificadora y la cadena payload, que es una cadena vacía si no se especificó.

citations.quote: includes the notification channel name, the notifying session's server process PID , and the payload string, which is an empty string if it has not been specified

sentences.text: Si NOTIFY se ejecuta dentro de una transacción, los eventos de notificación no se entregan hasta que la transacción se confirma.

citations.quote: if a NOTIFY is executed inside a transaction, the notify events are not delivered until and unless the transaction is committed

sentences.text: LISTEN tiene efecto al confirmar la transacción.

citations.quote: LISTEN takes effect at transaction commit

sentences.text: Para dejar de escuchar un canal se usa UNLISTEN, que cancela el registro de la sesión actual como oyente en ese canal.

citations.quote: UNLISTEN cancels any existing registration of the current PostgreSQL session as a listener on the notification channel named channel

sentences.text: El comodín * en UNLISTEN cancela todos los registros de escucha de la sesión actual.

citations.quote: The special wildcard * cancels all listener registrations for the current session

sentences.text: Al final de cada sesión, UNLISTEN * se ejecuta automáticamente.

citations.quote: At the end of each session, UNLISTEN * is automatically executed

questions.question: How do I dump a single database in the custom format and restore it in parallel?

questions.question: ¿Cómo actualizo un cluster de una versión mayor a otra con pg_upgrade?

Upgrades can be performed in minutes, particularly with --link mode

sentences.text: pg_upgrade admite actualizaciones desde 9.2.X y posteriores a la versión mayor actual de PostgreSQL, incluidas instantáneas y versiones beta.

citations.quote: supports upgrades from 9.2.X and later to the current major release of PostgreSQL , including snapshot and beta releases

sentences.text: Como paso opcional, se puede mover el clúster antiguo; si el directorio de instalación no es específico de la versión, es necesario mover el directorio actual de instalación de PostgreSQL para que no interfiera con la nueva instalación.

citations.quote: Copy any custom full text search files (dictionary, synonym, thesaurus, stop words) from the old to the new cluster

set authentication to peer in pg_hba.conf or use a ~/.pgpass file

sentences.text: La migración de slots lógicos solo se admite cuando el clúster antiguo es versión 17.0 o posterior; los slots lógicos de clústeres anteriores a 17.0 se ignoran silenciosamente.

citations.quote: CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW defines a materialized view of a query.

sentences.text: Materialized views in PostgreSQL use the rule system like views do, but persist the results in a table-like form.

sentences.text: Unlike a table created with CREATE TABLE AS, the materialized view cannot subsequently be directly updated.

sentences.text: REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW completely replaces the contents of a materialized view, and if WITH DATA is specified (or defaults) the backing query is executed to provide the new data and the materialized view is left in a scannable state.

If WITH DATA is specified (or defaults) the backing query is executed to provide the new data, and the materialized view is left in a scannable state.
